gary_2026_10_01_reciprocal_founders_roun.title: Reciprocal Founders Roundtable (40 & Over)
gary_2026_10_01_reciprocal_founders_roun.label: Startup / Business
gary_2026_10_01_reciprocal_founders_roun.summary: Gary's Guide: Seen Enough to Know the Risks. Crazy Enough to Take Them. A small roundtable for founders who grew out of hustle culture & kept building anyway. Bring one conversation you've been avoiding. Leave with a clearer view of it, & a handful of founders who know what you're dealing with. No stage. No audience. No pitching. Nothing said here leaves the room. Facilitated by executive coach Daniel Stillman, author of Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter. Who is this for? You're not 25 with nothing to lose. You have a mortgage. You'd like a real vacation this year. Maybe your parents need more of you than they used to. And you still have something you want to build. The hustle story doesn't fit that life. The ambition didn't go anywhere. Why a Roundtable? You've been to the big mixer. You've sat through the panel you could have watched on YouTube at 2x. This is a small, off-the-record table where every person talks & every person gets heard. Founders get honest faster when there's no one to perform for. The Conversation Our lives are built by the conversations we have, & defined by the ones we avoid. The cofounder conflict you brush off every week. The hire you won't admit isn't working. The pivot that's been "next quarter" for 3 quarters. The runway number you haven't said out loud. The hardest ones are with yourself. The bargain you made years ago & never renegotiated. The anxiety you can't politely ask to leave. An avoided conversation doesn't disappear. It goes underground & gets more expensive. Bring one. How to get a seat Admission is by application, & the questions are the prework. Give them real answers. That's how we build the table. We pick people who are building right now & who care about the other founders' problems as much as their own. One house rule: if you're accepted & don't show, you won't be invited back. The Format 5 rounds, in order: Who's here. Who you are & why you're building what you're building. The avoided conversation. Each person puts theirs on the table: the conflict or tension they're sitting with. Stories over advice. The group answers with what happened to them. Nobody tries to fix you. Asks & offers. One thing you need from the group. One thing you can give. Close. What you're taking with you, & what you'll do about it. The Follow Up: You'll join an ongoing thread with the people at your table. Send the resource you promised. Ask the follow-up you thought of on the train home. Your Co-Hosts Daniel Stillman designs conversations for a living, & insists that you do too. He's an executive coach & facilitator who works with founders & founding teams on how they lead, communicate, & navigate the conversations that matter. He hosts The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management podcast) & wrote Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter, a handbook for changemakers & innovators. Anson Wu is the founder of Ugly Talk, the no-BS event series where battle-tested founders share the setbacks, pivots, & lessons behind the wins. Since 2019 it's grown across New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami. Anson also runs Grey Journal, the digital media company behind it, & came up as a designer & agency founder. By his own description, a recovering underthinker still mining the lessons from two failed startups. About Ugly Talk Started in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough aha! moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com

gary_2026_10_06_tech_x_market_decoders_l.title: Tech x Market Decoders - Let's Talk About Jev
gary_2026_10_06_tech_x_market_decoders_l.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_06_tech_x_market_decoders_l.summary: Gary's Guide: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, & it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.summary: Gary's Guide: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneurs We are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

jc_culture_44040_2026_10_03_free_diapers.summary: Please Take Our Ad: Community Giving Luvs is bringing its Give Back Billboard to Jersey City, turning an advertisement into an opportunity to directly support local families with free diapers. From 12–6 p.m., families can visit Mary McLeod Bethune Park and take part in an interactive billboard made from Luvs diaper packs. As the packs are removed, the billboard will gradually reveal the message: “Leak protection shouldn’t be a luxury.” For 50 years, Luvs has stood for value, and as families face the rising cost of raising children, the brand is bringing that commitment directly to the community through free diapers, giveaways and more. One free box of diapers per household, while supplies last. Sizes subject to availability. No purchase necessary.

On the first and second Wednesdays of each month, enjoy live entertainment that adds to the vibrant, community atmosphere of the market. Whether you’re shopping for the week, grabbing a bite, or simply enjoying the park, the Hamilton Park Farmers Market is a welcoming space to connect with local vendors and neighbors.

jc_culture_10003572_2026_10_14_hamilton_.summary: Join us at the Hamilton Park Farmers Market, your midweek destination for fresh, local, and thoughtfully crafted food and goods. Each week, we’re proud to feature farm-fresh produce from Stony Hill Farm alongside a curated selection of specialty vendors. Browse a variety of offerings including our long time vendor Pickles and Olives, fresh seafood from Scale Fish Market, and prepared foods perfect for dinner. You can also find baked goods, candles, personal care products, and more. You can even take advantage of convenient services like on-site knife sharpening while you shop. On the first and second Wednesdays of each month, enjoy live entertainment that adds to the vibrant, community atmosphere of the market. Whether you’re shopping for the week, grabbing a bite, or simply enjoying the park, the Hamilton Park Farmers Market is a welcoming space to connect with local vendors and neighbors.
